target.title: fix: Control UI avatar initial breaks on emoji display names
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent's display name begins with an emoji or other astral Unicode character, the Control UI sidebar avatar rendered a broken or garbled initial (a lone UTF-16 surrogate half / replacement character) instead of the intended glyph.
- Solution: Replaced `(label || agent.id).slice(0, 1).toUpperCase()` (first UTF-16 code unit) with a new `deriveAvatarInitial` helper that uses `String.fromCodePoint(value.codePointAt(0))` (first full code point), returning `""` for empty or missing names.
- What changed: `ui/src/lib/avatar.ts` — new exported `deriveAvatarInitial`; `ui/src/components/app-sidebar.ts` now uses it.
- What did NOT change: Behavior for ordinary ASCII names; other `.slice()` sites were intentionally left unchanged because they operate on ASCII-only inputs (hex UUIDs, commit SHAs, ASCII-stripped build IDs) and are not surrogate-unsafe.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The avatar initial for emoji-initial display names was a dangling UTF-16 surrogate; it is now the full code point (a single glyph).
- **Real environment tested:** Direct node function call against the patched module on branch `fix/control-ui-avatar-initial-utf16`, using `node --import tsx`; did not boot a full OpenClaw runtime (pure string helper).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx avatar-evidence.ts
  # avatar-evidence.ts imports the exported deriveAvatarInitial and calls it on sample inputs.
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  deriveAvatarInitial("😀Name") = "😀" (expected "😀") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("🚀") = "🚀" (expected "🚀") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("Bob") = "B" (expected "B") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("") = "" (expected "") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial(null) = "" (expected "") OK
  deriveAvatarInitial("  ") = " " (expected " ") OK
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Emoji/astral initials are preserved as a single glyph; ASCII names are uppercased to their first char; empty/null input yields `""`.
- **What was not tested:** Did not start a live OpenClaw UI instance; only exercised the patched `deriveAvatarInitial` function locally (per guide §4 degradation for pure utility functions).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `ui/src/lib/avatar.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: emoji-initial name → first code point; ASCII → uppercased first char; empty/null → `""`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Locks the exact code-point (not code-unit) contract that the sidebar renders, which is the precise defect.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: The avatar initial used `.slice(0, 1)`, which takes the first UTF-16 code unit. An astral code point such as an emoji occupies two code units, so the slice split it in half and yielded a dangling surrogate.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No code-point-aware initial-derivation helper.

target.title: fix(retry): avoid status code substring matches

Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users encountering permanent provider errors or multi-hour rate limits would have the session retry up to three times, re-sending the same context even though the error cannot clear within the retry window.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retryable HTTP status codes now match only standalone status tokens, so model identifiers, image dimensions, and API keys cannot accidentally trigger retries. The classifier also recognizes daily limits and hour/day retry windows as non-retryable, while preserving normal transient 429 and 5xx handling.

## User Impact

Sessions now stop promptly for permanent provider failures and long-lived quotas instead of making additional doomed calls. Transient provider and network failures keep their existing retry behavior.

target.title: fix(usage-bar): bound numeric verb arguments
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `fixed` and `meter` parse operator-authored numeric arguments with `Number.parseInt`, accepting partial tokens and allowing meter width to control synchronous loop and output size without an upper bound.
- Solution: reuse the shared strict-integer parser and enforce `fixed` precision `0..20` and `meter` width `1..100` at the translator boundary.
- What changed: focused translator guards plus regression coverage for invalid tokens, invalid ranges, and valid boundary values.
- What was not changed: the usage template schema, template file loader, built-in footer, valid default arguments, or reply delivery beyond usage-line selection.

## What Problem This Solves

`messages.usageTemplate` is operator-authored data. Its interpolation strings reach the synchronous usage footer renderer on every eligible full-usage reply. Before this patch, `meter:12junk` was treated as width 12, while an all-digit width directly controlled loop iterations, array growth, and output length before the renderer could reach its fallback boundary.

`fixed:101` is already contained by `renderUsageBar`'s outer catch and falls back instead of escaping through the reply. This patch still rejects that invalid precision before calling `toFixed`, but the confirmed availability risk is the unbounded `meter` construction.

## User Impact

Invalid custom usage templates now fail quickly and select the existing built-in usage footer instead of performing width-proportional work or applying partially parsed arguments. Existing templates using the documented/default values continue to render unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #89835, which introduced the native templated usage footer renderer and its `fixed` / `meter` verbs.
- **Gap this fills:** the original translator added the verbs without strict numeric-token parsing or owner-defined resource bounds.
- **Consistency:** keeps the existing fail-open contract: an invalid custom render is empty, and `resolveResponseUsageLine` selects the built-in formatted footer.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #105063 (closed).
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** it only guarded partial tokens, had no numeric upper bounds or regression tests, and was automatically closed because its author exceeded the active-PR limit.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** it reuses `parseStrictInteger` from `@openclaw/normalization-core`, caps both numeric verbs in their shared translator owner, and locks the valid and invalid boundaries in tests.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the production `resolveResponseUsageLine` path proves invalid inline config falls back immediately, including a billion-cell request and an unsafe-integer token, while valid controls still render.

## Merge risk

- **Why it matters / User impact:** prevents operator-configured footer data from causing unbounded synchronous meter construction on the reply path.
- **Risk labels considered:** availability, compatibility.
- **Risk explanation:** previously accepted but malformed or excessive verb arguments now produce the built-in footer instead of a custom render. Valid documented and built-in values remain within the bounds.
- **Why acceptable:** the diff is limited to one translator seam and its existing test file; defaults and valid boundary behavior are covered.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — current-main reachability, RED/GREEN tests, strict parser reuse, targeted format/lint/type checks, focused diff checks, and production-path runtime proof all passed.
- **Patch quality notes:** `translator.ts` is an existing large module; this patch deliberately avoids a broad unrelated split. Returning `""` for an invalid verb argument is the translator's established invalid-render signal consumed by the existing built-in footer selection, not a new downstream fallback.
- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts`
- **Root cause:** operator-authored verb tokens entered `applyVerb` as strings; `Number.parseInt` truncated partial tokens and no maximum was enforced, so `meter` looped, pushed cells, and joined output until reaching the supplied width.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the invariant is enforced once where `fixed` and `meter` arguments become numbers, before either formatter consumes them.
- **What did NOT change:** public schema/protocol/defaults; loader/watch behavior; reply transport and session logic; docs, lockfiles, and unrelated formatting. Out of scope: changing the template format or adding loader traversal.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `translator.ts` owns the DSL verb semantics; `normalization-core` owns shared strict integer token parsing. The guard is at that canonical boundary, before formatting. Related open PR scan found no open implementation; closed #105063 was assessed separately.
- **Scenario locked in:** partial, negative, scientific, unsafe, zero/out-of-range meter, and out-of-range fixed arguments fall back; `fixed:20` and `meter:100` remain valid.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** one shared bounded parser at the two numeric verb call sites prevents both permissive parsing and resource growth without changing the template format.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** strict, bounded numeric arguments for operator-configured `fixed` and `meter` usage-template verbs.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `messages.usageTemplate` inline/path config → config schema accepts template data → `loadUsageBarTemplate` → `resolveResponseUsageLine` → `renderUsageBar` / `applyVerb` → custom footer or built-in footer fallback.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime — actual production `resolveResponseUsageLine`, loader/translator contract, and built-in footer selection. The proof ends at that complete local boundary.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** reused `parseStrictInteger` from `@openclaw/normalization-core`. Repository search found built-in/documented values `fixed:4` and `meter:1/5`; the core-owned DSL bounds are `fixed 0..20` and `meter 1..100`.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, pnpm 11.2.2, current OpenClaw source at commit `0ab105b2abee6dc4d18c41d353c827c46be21c08`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** bounded proof invoked a TypeScript harness with `node --import tsx`, imported `resolveResponseUsageLine` from production source, supplied inline `messages.usageTemplate` values, asserted fallback/control outputs, and wrote evidence only after all assertions passed.
- **Evidence after fix:** BEFORE was captured on `origin/main`; AFTER and CONTROL were captured through the production usage-line path.

```text
BEFORE origin/main:
meter:100000:bar -> length=100000
meter:12junk:bar -> length=12
fixed:101 -> empty custom render (already contained by outer fallback)

AFTER 0ab105b2ab:
invalid_case_count=10
invalid_elapsed_ms=3.267
meter:1000000000 -> Usage: 100 in / 20 out
meter:9007199254740992 -> Usage: 100 in / 20 out
meter:12junk -> Usage: 100 in / 20 out
fixed:101 -> Usage: 100 in / 20 out

CONTROL:
fixed:2 -> 100.00
fixed:20 -> 100.00000000000000000000
meter:10 -> _____-----
meter:100 length -> 100
result=PASS
```

- **Observed result after fix:** invalid partial, negative, scientific, unsafe, and out-of-range tokens select the existing built-in footer in under 4 ms for the ten-case proof; valid maximum and normal values render normally.
- **What was not tested:** no boundary beyond `resolveResponseUsageLine` was in scope. The Blacksmith Testbox delegation was not used because the local `crabbox` binary failed its own sanity check. A local `check:changed` run passed its relevant guards and formatting, then stopped on a plugin SDK baseline mismatch from the rebased main snapshot; subsequent main commits refreshed that unrelated baseline.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Closed competing PR #105063 was reviewed for scope; this patch adds the missing range caps, shared-parser reuse, tests, and runtime proof.

## Regression Test Plan

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.ts src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts
pnpm exec oxlint --type-aware --type-check --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.ts src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:core:test
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 CI=1 pnpm check:changed
git diff --check
```

## Risk / Compatibility

Low risk. No API, schema, protocol, or default changes. The only compatibility change is intentional: invalid or excessive custom verb arguments now use the existing built-in fallback. Documented and built-in arguments are unchanged.

## What was not changed

- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: unchanged.
- Reply transport and session behavior outside the fixed path: unchanged.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: unchanged.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `fixed` and `meter` truncated operator-authored tokens with `Number.parseInt`; without an owner-defined maximum, `meter` performed width-proportional loop, array, and string work.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** strict parsing and range enforcement happen at the single translator boundary shared by both verbs, before `toFixed` or meter construction.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High.
- **Patch quality notes:** focused 2-file change with RED/GREEN coverage and production-path proof; no symptom-only downstream fallback was added.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** shared numeric token semantics come from `normalization-core`; DSL-specific ranges remain owned by the usage-bar translator.

target.title: fix(browser): do not sticky-adopt policy-blocked openTab targets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openTab` could sticky-adopt a tab whose **final** URL failed browser SSRF policy. Chrome MCP and CDP create-target paths set `runtime.lastTargetId` before `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed`. When a allowed request URL redirected to a private endpoint (for example `http://127.0.0.1/...`), `openTab` still rejected — but the blocked target stayed sticky for the next targetless browser action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Align Chrome MCP and CDP create-target adoption with the existing raw `/json/new` contract already documented in the same file: adopt `lastTargetId` only after post-navigation policy passes. Playwright `createPageViaPlaywright` already validates before returning, so it needed no change.

## User Impact

**Before:** A rejected redirect open could still become the implicit target for later snapshot/act calls that omit `targetId`.

**After:** Policy-blocked final URLs do not update `lastTargetId`; the next targetless action cannot land on that blocked tab via sticky selection.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-ops.ts` (Chrome MCP + CDP create-target sticky adoption)
- Sibling contract already present on raw `/json/new`: "Adopt only fully validated targets..."
- Regressions:
  - `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.existing-session.test.ts` (Chrome MCP)
  - `extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-selection-state.test.ts` (CDP create-target)

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.existing-session.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-selection-state.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |extension-browser| ... > does not sticky-adopt a CDP-created tab when the discovered URL is policy-blocked 17ms
 ✓ |extension-browser| ... > does not sticky-adopt a Chrome MCP tab when the final URL is policy-blocked 7ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 147.84s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Blocked post-navigation `openTab` results no longer sticky-adopt `lastTargetId` on Chrome MCP or CDP create-target paths.
- **Canonical reachability path:** Browser tool / control routes → profile `openTab` → Chrome MCP `openChromeMcpTab` or CDP `createTargetViaCdp` + `/json/list` discovery → `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed` → only then `runtime.lastTargetId = …`.
- **Boundary crossed:** External/redirected page URL → local sticky target selection used by targetless browser actions.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reuses existing `assertBrowserNavigationResultAllowed`; matches raw `/json/new` adopt-after-validate ordering. Does not add config/env.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node source checkout; production `openTab` caller with mocked Chrome MCP / CDP discovery returning a private final URL under default SSRF policy.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.existing-session.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.tab-selection-state.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text

 ✓ ... > does not sticky-adopt a Chrome MCP tab when the final URL is policy-blocked 7ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  28 passed (28)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Both paths reject the blocked final URL and leave `lastTargetId` unset / not equal to the blocked target id.
- **What was not tested:** Live Chrome redirect to loopback; closing the orphaned blocked tab after rejection; remote CDP Playwright path (already validates inside `createPageViaPlaywright`).

target.title: fix(slack): read resolved userToken with env fallback in channel type resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveSlackConversationInfo()` uses `account.config.userToken` to resolve the token for Slack API calls. `account.config.userToken` only contains the raw config value — it does **not** include the `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` environment variable fallback.

Users who set `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` env var without also configuring `channels.slack.accounts.<id>.userToken` in the config file get an empty token, causing channel type resolution to silently fall back to `"unknown"` for non-DM channels.

Additionally, even with the resolved `account.userToken`, the old token selection `account.botToken ?? account.userToken` always prefers botToken when both tokens exist. For mixed-token configurations (botToken + userToken both configured), `conversations.info` needs the read-scoped user token, but botToken was selected first when both exist.

A single read-selected client was also reused for native-IM `conversations.open`, which requires a write-scoped bot token.

## Changes

- `channel-type.ts`: use `resolveSlackOperationToken(account, "read")` for `conversations.info`
- `channel-type.ts`: use `resolveSlackOperationToken(account, "write")` for native-IM `conversations.open`
- Instantiate separate Slack clients after branching instead of sharing one read token client
- Tests assert the exact token passed to `createSlackWebClient` for mixed-token read/write paths

Credit: Finding identified by [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103468#issuecomment-4934650079).

## Evidence

**Current head:** `3b83e4b8`

**Unit tests (18/18 passed):**
```
pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
pnpm exec oxlint extensions/slack/src/channel-type.ts extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/slack/src/channel-type.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

New/updated regression coverage:
1. prefers userToken over botToken for channel type reads (mixed-token account) ✅
2. uses write token for native IM `conversations.open` (mixed-token account) ✅
3. does not reuse native IM peer metadata across mixed-token bot rotation ✅
4. falls back to botToken when no userToken is configured ✅
5. returns unknown when neither botToken nor userToken is available ✅

**Rank-up (P2 cache identity):** native IM cache key now uses the same effective write token as `conversations.open`, so bot-token rotation cannot serve stale DM peer metadata.

**Lint:** `pnpm exec oxlint` — no errors

**Format:** `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` — clean

**After-fix live Slack proof (redacted):**

```
Current head: 7c3fb919
Token prefixes: bot=xoxb-***, user=xoxp-***

Public channel C0***3T via user read token:
  ok=true, type=channel, name=zw1, is_private=false

Private channel C0***DT via user read token:

  ok=true, channelId=D0***, user=U0B***

Native IM open via user read token on D0***:

```

This shows the fix path: read-scoped user token classifies non-DM channels successfully, while write-scoped bot token opens native IM; the read-only user token correctly fails write-scoped `conversations.open`.

- Mixed-token regression coverage added

target.title: fix(feishu): cancel agent runs when source messages are recalled
target.body:
Related: #55691
Related: #81997

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users could recall or withdraw a message but OpenClaw would still continue processing that source message and run the agent/tools. This could happen when the recall event arrived while the original message was already debounced, queued, or inside an agent dispatch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu recall handling previously only showed up indirectly at reply delivery time, when sending a reply to a missing/recalled message could fail. This change handles the inbound `im.message.recalled_v1` event at the channel boundary, records the recalled source message in a Feishu-local runtime context, skips recalled messages before dispatch, and binds active dispatches to an abort signal so in-flight runs stop instead of producing replies.

Live testing also showed that some Feishu app configurations may not deliver `im.message.recalled_v1` to the plugin, while Feishu's message reaction API still returns code `231003` (`message not found / maybe deleted`) when the typing target is the recalled source message. The Feishu dispatcher now treats that specific channel-local signal as a conservative fallback only when the missing typing target is the inbound source message, then reuses the same recall registry, abort signal, and reply-suppression path.

The state is process-local and bounded because it only needs to coordinate nearby receive/debounce/dispatch timing within one gateway process. It does not add a core API or persistent storage surface.

## User Impact

When a Feishu user withdraws a message, OpenClaw now treats that source message as cancelled. Pending debounced messages are dropped when the recall event is delivered, active single-agent and broadcast dispatches receive an abort signal, and final replies are suppressed if the recall or missing-source fallback lands before delivery.

## Evidence

AI-assisted change.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/typing.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/reply-dispatcher.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.message-handler.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/monitor.reaction.test.ts`
  - 5 files passed, 243 tests passed.

target.title: fix(codex): keep progress replies from ending active turns
target.body:
Related: #100153

Alternative to #100156.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex with `message_tool_only` source delivery could receive a progress or acknowledgment reply and then see the active turn end before the promised work or final answer was completed.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds explicit delivery intent to current-source `message(action=send)` calls for Codex `message_tool_only` runs. Sends with `final: false` or an omitted `final` remain visible but non-terminal; only a successfully delivered current-source send with `final: true` releases the turn.

The prompt and delivery hints tell the model to use commentary for ordinary progress and `final: true` only after requested work and verification are complete. The internal `final` field is removed before provider delivery. Other runtimes, delivery modes, channels, and explicit cross-chat sends retain their existing behavior.

This is a structural alternative to #100156. That PR reduces the failure through prompt steering; this change keeps the runtime safe when a model still sends a progress message through the message tool.

## User Impact

Codex-backed users can receive a visible progress message without losing the rest of the active turn. Completed final replies still terminate cleanly, preserving duplicate-reply prevention and normal turn release.

## Evidence

Before the change, a real Telegram direct-chat turn on macOS with OpenClaw 2026.7.2, Codex app-server, `message_tool_only`, and GPT-5.6 followed this sequence:

```text
message(action=send) progress reply
tool result: delivered
turn.dynamic_tool_terminal_release
session ended successfully before the promised investigation
```

Live Telegram verification after the change:

- `message(action=send, final=false)` delivered `PROGRESS_SENT`.
- The same turn continued through a 10-second wait and a Git status tool call.
- `message(action=send, final=true)` delivered `FINAL_SENT`.
- `turn.dynamic_tool_terminal_release` occurred only after `FINAL_SENT`.
- The session ended successfully with no abort or timeout.
- A separate natural five-minute investigation completed 19 tool calls and delivered its full diagnosis with `final=true`.

target.title: fix(config): mark pre-update snapshot only after a successful write
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` records the config path in a process-global "already snapshotted" set **before** it reads and writes the snapshot. If that first attempt fails transiently — a temporary file lock, an `EBUSY`, a momentary permission hiccup — the path is nonetheless marked done, so **no snapshot is ever taken for the rest of the process** and the operator silently loses their pre-update rollback point (#105193).

## Why This Change Was Made

The early mark was a guard against looping "on every later write". But `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` is only invoked once per `openclaw update` (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command.ts`), not on ordinary config writes — so the loop it guarded against does not occur, while the cost (dropping the snapshot on a transient first failure) is a real data-integrity gap.

The fix moves the `preUpdateConfigSnapshotsWritten.add(...)` to **after** a successful write. On failure the path stays unmarked, so the next update attempt retries. Successful behavior is unchanged: the first successful call marks the path and later calls in the same process remain no-ops (the existing "once per process" and "survives multiple config writes" tests still pass).

## User Impact

- A transient failure on the first pre-update snapshot attempt no longer permanently disables snapshots; the operator keeps a rollback point on the next update.
- No behavior change on the success path or for the per-update (non-looping) call pattern.

## Evidence

**Regression test** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts` → 9/9): `createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot retries after a transient first-attempt failure (#105193)` injects a `readFile` that throws `EBUSY` on the first call; it asserts no snapshot exists and the path is not marked, then a second call (read now succeeds) writes the `.pre-update` snapshot with the original content.

**Discriminator**: reverting only `backup-rotation.ts` (restoring mark-before-I/O) fails the new test — the second attempt is skipped because the path was marked on the failed first attempt, exactly the reported permanent block.

Fixes #105193

target.title: fix(bedrock-mantle): isolate discovery cache by credential
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a long-lived OpenClaw process, Bedrock Mantle model discovery cached results keyed only by AWS region. After switching bearer tokens / accounts in the same region within the TTL window, the second discovery reused the first credential's model catalog without contacting Mantle. New accounts could see the wrong model list, and names from a prior account could linger across an authorization boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`discoverMantleModels` treated `region` as a sufficient cache key, but the `/v1/models` response is credential-scoped. The owner boundary is the discovery cache itself: isolate entries by a non-reversible SHA-256 fingerprint of the bearer token combined with the normalized region. TTL, endpoints, error fallback, and model normalization are unchanged. Fingerprints stay private to the module and are never logged or exported.

## User Impact

**Before:** Same region + different bearer token within TTL could return the previous token's cached models (one fetch).
**After:** Same region + different bearer token misses cache and re-discovers; same region + same token still hits cache.

## Evidence

- Base: `34205aabf9b918ddcf0845163404d68fc8dbd22e` (`origin/main`)
- Head: `f756d1ff216fa1040a1cb0b3dc568f275cb1ebc7`

- Platform: Windows

- Existing: `"returns cached models on subsequent calls within refresh interval"` still asserts same-token cache hit

- Competitor search (`bedrock mantle discovery cache` / `mantle discovery credential`): no open duplicates
- **Not tested:** live AWS Mantle `/v1/models` with real credentials (deterministic fetch mock is sufficient for cache isolation)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Mantle discovery cache no longer returns another credential's model catalog when only the region matches.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, worktree `codex/mantle-discovery-cache-credentials` at `f756d1ff`, vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): derive heap thresholds from V8 heap size limit (#104631)
target.body:
Closes #104631

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the gateway with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size` above the default (e.g. 8 GB on a 15 GB RAM host) receive false-positive `heap_threshold` critical memory pressure diagnostics as soon as `heapUsedBytes` reaches 2 GB, even when the V8 heap limit has 75%+ headroom and the system has abundant free memory.

This triggers unnecessary diagnostic events, log noise, and stability bundle writes, and can cause downstream monitoring or supervisor restart chains (the linked issue reports a gateway drain-and-restart sequence on the reporter's setup).

## Why This Change Was Made

The diagnostic memory classifier previously hardcoded heap pressure thresholds at 1 GiB (warning) and 2 GiB (critical) — values that were reasonable for Node's default `--max-old-space-size` (~2 GB server / ~4 GB desktop) but do not scale when operators configure a larger heap limit.

This change derives default heap warning and critical thresholds from V8's effective `heap_size_limit`, so they automatically adapt to whatever `--max-old-space-size` is set:

- **Critical**: 75% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 2 GiB
- **Warning**: 60% of the V8 heap limit, floored at 1 GiB

The conservative lower bounds ensure small-heap or default-heap environments remain equally protected. RSS threshold and RSS growth detection are unchanged. No configuration key is added — the fix is fully automatic.

## User Impact

Users on decently-provisioned hosts (e.g. `--max-old-space-size=8192`) no longer see spurious `heap_threshold` critical pressure from routine heap usage at 2 GB, while the same protection level is preserved for default or constrained heap sizes. The change is invisible to operators: no new config, no migration, no restart requirement beyond the usual update.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

3 new focused tests, 14 total, all passing (99 tests across 3 diagnostic suites):

| Test | What it proves |
|------|---------------|
| `default heap thresholds never go below the original constants as a conservative lower bound (#104631)` | Adaptive defaults floor at 1 GiB / 2 GiB — small-heap protection unchanged |
| `emits heap_threshold at the adaptive default warning threshold (#104631)` | Warning fires at 60% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |
| `emits heap_threshold critical at the adaptive default critical threshold (#104631)` | Critical fires at 75% of the real V8 `heap_size_limit` |

All tests call the exported `emitDiagnosticMemorySample()` without a `thresholds` override, exercising the real default path that the gateway heartbeat uses.

### Real-behavior proof

Two experiments were conducted on a real gateway process (Node v24.13.1, OpenClaw 2026.7.2 with fix applied). A `--import` preload monkey-patch injected controlled `process.memoryUsage()` values — the heartbeat and classifier code paths are fully production, only the OS memory input is replaced (equivalent to the `memoryUsage` parameter seam the function already exposes for testing).

#### Experiment A: Adaptive `heap_threshold` fires through the real diagnostics path

Gateway started with default V8 heap limit (~4.19 GB) and `diagnostics.memoryPressureSnapshot: true`. The monkey-patch returns `heapUsed=3.3 GB` (above the adaptive critical threshold of 3.14 GB = 4.19 GB * 0.75), `rss=2.8 GB` (below the fixed 3 GB RSS critical threshold, so `rss_threshold` does not preempt).

After ~27 seconds, the heartbeat detected the condition and produced:

```
[diagnostics/memory] level=critical reason=heap_threshold
  rss=2.8 GiB heap=3.3 GiB threshold=3.14 GiB thresholdRatio=105.1%
  memoryPressureSnapshot=enabled
critical memory pressure bundle written: ... reason=heap_threshold level=critical
```

**Confirms:** The adaptive threshold (75% of V8 heap limit) correctly classifies above-threshold heap use through the real gateway heartbeat, diagnostics log, and stability bundle path.

#### Experiment B: No false-positive under enlarged heap (8 GB limit, simulating reporter's environment)

Gateway started with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` (~8.19 GB V8 heap limit). The monkey-patch returns `heapUsed=2.2 GB` (the reporter's actual heap level; below the adaptive warning threshold of 4.91 GB = 8.19 GB * 0.6), `rss=1.0 GB` (below both RSS thresholds).

The gateway ran for **~10 minutes** with zero `heap_threshold` or `rss_threshold` critical events:

```
17:56:31 [heartbeat] started
^C18:06:22 [gateway] received SIGINT; shutting down
```

No `diagnostics/memory` pressure events appeared in the log during the entire run.

**Confirms:** The false-positive `heap_threshold critical` that would have fired at 2 GiB under the old hardcoded threshold is eliminated on an 8 GB heap. The adaptive thresholds (60%/75% of V8 heap limit) correctly classify 2.2 GB heap usage as no pressure on an ~8.19 GB heap.

```
const GB = 1024 * 1024 * 1024;
const MB = 1024 * 1024;

process.memoryUsage = () => {
  return {

    heapTotal: 3.5 * GB,
    heapUsed: 3.3 * GB,  // above 3.14 GB, heap_threshold critical fires
    external: 100 * MB,
    arrayBuffers: 10 * MB,
  };
};
```

target.title: fix(tool-call-repair): parse JSON-format plain-text tool calls alongside bracket/XML/Harmony
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits tool calls as plain JSON text (e.g. `{"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"location": "Paris"}}`) instead of through the native `tool_calls` response field, OpenClaw's plain-text tool-call repair fails to promote it into an executable tool call. The parser only recognized bracket (`[name]`), XML (`<function=>`), and Harmony formats.

Additionally, three related gaps fixed:

- **Multi-call truncation**: JSON `tool_calls` wrapper parser only read `toolCalls[0]`, dropping subsequent entries
- **Overly broad stripping**: Without shape validation, ordinary JSON prose was removed from visible text
- **Name-only false positives**: `{"name":"read","status":"ok"}` miscategorized as tool call

Affects Ollama, LM Studio, xAI via `createPlainTextToolCallCompatWrapper`. Observed with Qwen family models.

Fixes #99251

## Why This Change Was Made

**Payload parser** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.ts`):
- `readJsonToolName`, `hasJsonToolArgs`, `readJsonToolArguments` — multi-field name/args extraction
- `extractJsonToolCallNameAndArgs` returns array — multi-tool wrappers promote all valid entries
- Atomic wrapper rejection: any malformed entry → entire `tool_calls` array rejected
- Non-record argument rejection: arrays/strings/primitives rejected, not coerced
- `parseJsonToolCallBlocksAt` — scans `{`, validates via `JSON.parse`, requires tool-call shape
- Pre-scan gate: `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` disables JSON stripping when mixed with prose

**Stream normalizer** (`packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.ts`):
- JSON key-based detection for incomplete streaming chunks

## User Impact

- Models returning JSON tool calls in `content` now execute tools correctly
- Multi-tool wrappers promote all entries, not just the first
- Ordinary JSON prose preserved; name-only JSON not falsely classified

## Evidence

### Unit tests
```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts → 28 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/tool-call-repair/src/stream-normalizer.test.ts → 99 passed
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts → 62 passed
```

### Deepseek live proof (real model → parser)
Provider: `deepseek` (`api.deepseek.com`), route: OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions`, model: `deepseek-v4-flash`

| Pattern | Model response | Result |
|---------|---------------|--------|
| tool_calls wrapper | `{"tool_calls":[{"function":{"name":"get_weather","arguments":{"city":"Beijing","units":"celsius"}}}]}` | ✓ 1 block |
| Flat standalone | `{"name":"read","arguments":{"path":"/etc/hosts"}}` | ✓ 1 block |
| Multi-tool wrapper | 2-entry `tool_calls` array | ✓ 2 blocks |

Edge cases (mixed prose, name-only JSON): 4/4 passed.

### Lint & format

```
oxfmt --check → clean
```

### Branch
Rebased onto upstream/main (2026-07-12), no conflicts.

- ✅ State observed route — OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` on `api.deepseek.com`

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): honor deadline and skip supplement exhaustive fallback
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`memory_search` with `corpus="wiki"` or `corpus="all"` can miss the 15s tool deadline when digest-selected candidates underfill `maxResults`. The wiki supplement then falls through to a full-vault Markdown scan (25–27s on large vaults), so recall times out and host work may continue after the tool already failed. Fixes #104719.

## Root Cause / Fix

- Root cause: `searchWikiCorpus()` treated missing or underfilled digest hits as a signal to enumerate/parse the entire vault, and the memory tool deadline signal never reached the supplement path.
- Fix:
  1. Propagate `deadlineSignal` through `MemoryCorpusSupplement.search` → wiki supplement → `searchMemoryWiki` / `searchWikiCorpus`.
  2. Supplement path sets `exhaustiveFallback: false` so digest underfill does not trigger full-vault scanning. Direct `wiki_search` keeps exhaustive fallback.
  3. Shared page reads use **bounded (16) abort-before-claim workers** (not sequential): deadlines stop claiming new paths while direct exhaustive search keeps parallel throughput. In-flight reads settle.

## Evidence

### Production function proof (`node --import tsx`)

Multi-page vault exercise of the real `searchMemoryWiki` / `readQueryableWikiPages` path (see Real behavior proof for captured output). Covers:

- default exhaustive hit still works
- `exhaustiveFallback: false` skips vault scan without digest
- pre-aborted signal returns `[]`
- mid-batch abort stops claiming further page reads (`abort_stopped_early`)

### Regression tests

- `"skips full-vault fallback when exhaustiveFallback is false (#104719)"`
- `"returns early when the deadline signal is already aborted (#104719)"`
- `"reads wiki pages with bounded concurrency and stops claiming after abort (#104719)"` — asserts peak concurrency in (1, 16] and fewer reads than file count after abort
- `"forwards deadline signal and disables exhaustive fallback for supplement search (#104719)"`

### Test runner

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/corpus-supplement.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/query.test.ts -t "104719|exhaustiveFallback|already aborted|bounded concurrency|finds wiki pages by title"
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** memory-wiki supplement skips full-vault fallback after digest underfill, honors the memory_search deadline AbortSignal, and shared wiki page reads use bounded abort-aware concurrency instead of serial I/O.
**Environment tested:** Windows Node 22+, local checkout of `fix/issue-104719-wiki-deadline`, `node --import tsx`, vitest via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
**Steps run after the patch:** Created a temporary 40-page wiki vault; ran production `searchMemoryWiki` / `readQueryableWikiPages` with default search, `exhaustiveFallback: false`, pre-abort, and mid-batch abort; ran targeted vitest regressions including the bounded-concurrency abort test.
**Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "direct_hit_path": "sources/page-01.md",
  "direct_hits": 10,
  "direct_ms": 210,
  "file_count": 40,
  "abort_pages": 23,
  "abort_stopped_early": true,
  "supplement_no_digest": [],
  "preabort": [],
  "ok": true
}
```

**Observed result:** Default search still finds wiki pages; supplement-without-digest returns no vault scan; pre-abort returns empty; mid-batch abort stops claiming new paths (`abort_stopped_early: true`) while peak concurrency stays bounded (≤16). Targeted vitest regressions pass.
**Not tested:** Live gateway `memory_search` against a real ~77MB / 1200+ page compiled-wiki vault end-to-end (no such vault in this environment); Discord/Telegram delivery.

## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact

- Type: bug fix
- Scope: memory-wiki supplement + memory-core deadline plumbing + abort-aware bounded page reader (S)
- Security: none (no auth/credential changes); reduces unbounded host I/O after tool timeout without serializing exhaustive search

target.title: fix(hooks): bound HOOK.md reads during hook install validation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHookNameFromDir` in `src/hooks/install.ts` reads `HOOK.md` with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A malicious or malformed hook package containing a multi-gigabyte `HOOK.md` could force the install path to buffer the entire file into memory just to extract the hook name from frontmatter, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

`HOOK.md` is only parsed for a short frontmatter block (name, description). A 1 MiB cap is generous headroom for legitimate hook documentation while preventing the install path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector.

## User Impact

Installing a hook package with an oversized `HOOK.md` now fails fast with a clear size-limit error instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a `1 MiB + 1` byte `HOOK.md` and asserts `installHooksFromPath` rejects with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/install.test.ts --run` passes (29/29 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I wrote a standalone Node script (`/tmp/proof-101469.mjs`) that imports the real `installHooksFromPath` from `src/hooks/install.ts`, creates two bare hook directories under `/tmp`, and exercises the code path directly. The script uses `inspection: "package-kind"` to avoid install-policy and target-availability side effects while still going through `resolveHookNameFromDir`, where the bounded `HOOK.md` read lives.

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101469.mjs
== PR 101469 real behavior proof ==
workDir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461
HOOK.md size limit: 1048576 bytes

-- Normal case: small HOOK.md --
hookDir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/normal-hook
result: {
  "ok": true,
  "hookPackId": "normal-hook",
  "hooks": [
    "normal-hook"
  ],
  "packageKind": "hook-only",
  "targetDir": "/tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/hooks/normal-hook"
}

-- Oversized case: HOOK.md = 1 MiB + 1 byte --
hookDir: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/oversized-hook
HOOK.md bytes: 1048577
error: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461/oversized-hook/HOOK.md
PASS: oversized HOOK.md rejected before downstream processing

-- Cleanup --
removed /tmp/openclaw-proof-101469-1783419986824-2374461
```

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: [codex] Fix cron chat session-key binding
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #81375.

- Stop the cron tool from stamping the caller chat `sessionKey` onto implicit `sessionTarget="main"` / `payload.kind="systemEvent"` jobs.
- Preserve explicit `job.sessionKey` and preserve caller-session stamping for isolated `agentTurn` jobs, where the run-scoped cron session and inferred announce delivery still need that context.
- Add regression coverage for both paths.

## Root Cause / Live Behavior

Observed on 2026-05-13 after a macOS restart with local OpenClaw `2026.5.10-beta.1` (`dedc49c`):

- WhatsApp was healthy, linked, connected, and running.
- A user WhatsApp `hi` was ingested at 11:08:08 BST (`web-inbound`, `web-auto-reply`, and `gateway/channels/whatsapp/inbound` all logged it), but no visible reply was delivered and typing later timed out.
- Two due cron jobs created from the same chat were bound to `sessionTarget="main"`, `payload.kind="systemEvent"`, and the WhatsApp direct-chat session key. Startup catch-up put that cron work on the same session lane as the human DM; one job ran from about 11:06:35 to 11:08:39, and the next started immediately afterward.
- Editing the live jobs to isolated `agentTurn` + announce delivery removed the lane collision. The WhatsApp channel stayed healthy and later outbound delivery succeeded.

I checked current upstream/latest beta before patching. `2026.5.12-beta.4` includes the adjacent WhatsApp pending-debounce close fix (#81246), and upstream main includes the active-run stuck-lane diagnostic fix (#81302), but neither changes this cron-tool session-key stamping behavior.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:


target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files

## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

target.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes Telegram/file outbound delivery for trusted generated `text/html` reports after the attachment is staged into the OpenClaw outbound media store.

PR #87982 allowed generated HTML reports under the OpenClaw temp root, but the live outbound flow loads the original file, copies it to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<uuid>.html`, then the channel adapter loads that staged copy again. The second load no longer lives under the temp root, so host-read rejected it and the Telegram message was silently dropped.

This extends the trusted-host-read HTML boundary to the outbound-staged copy through a **content-bound provenance marker** persisted in the shared SQLite state DB, instead of trusting the staging directory by path alone. Trust is bound to the exact staged bytes and verified read-once at host-read time.

Fixes #90557.

## Design

When `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` stages a file whose source was a trusted-generated HTML path (under the temp root), it records a provenance row in a new `outbound_media_provenance` table keyed by the staged file's realpath, storing the `sha256` + `size_bytes` of the staged bytes (`kind = "trusted-generated-html"`, `version = 1`).

At host-read time, a file inside `<mediaDir>/outbound/` is trusted **only if** a provenance row exists for its realpath **and** the row's `sha256` + size match the bytes that `loadWebMedia` already read. Files under the temp root keep their existing unconditional trust. The provenance row is pruned in lockstep with the staged file by `pruneStaleTrustedGeneratedHtmlMarkers`, wired into the media-store retention pass (`cleanOldMedia`).

Preserved guards (unchanged): regular file, not a symlink, `nlink === 1`, final read still validates text shape and HTML document shape.

## ClawSweeper P1 resolution

Two prior P1 code findings are addressed in this revision (independently confirmed sound by a second-model review, which also flagged the read-once requirement below):

- **Path-keyed provenance bypass** → **content-bound + read-once.** The marker now stores `sha256` + `size_bytes`, and host-read trust is decided by hashing the **same buffer `loadWebMedia` already read** (no second filesystem read, so there is no hash-then-read TOCTOU window). A file whose bytes are replaced after the marker is written is rejected. New regression test: stage bytes `B1` + mark with the real digest, overwrite the same path with different bytes `B2`, assert host-read is rejected with `path-not-allowed`.
- **Swallowed marker write failure** → **propagate.** `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` no longer swallows `markTrustedGeneratedHtmlPath` errors; on failure it best-effort unlinks the staged file and rethrows, so an infrastructure/write error surfaces through the normal media-failure path instead of deferring to a later silent Telegram reload drop. New test asserts the rethrow and the best-effort `rm`.

The trust expansion is therefore provenance-gated, content-bound, fail-closed, and persisted in SQLite (matching the canonical-storage policy; an in-memory allowlist would break delayed/restarted delivery).

## Test plan

```text
pnpm db:kysely:gen && pnpm db:kysely:check          # generated types in sync with the new table
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
```

## Real behavior proof

### Deterministic real-code-path before/after (2026-06-24)

This exercises the **same production helpers the Telegram channel adapter uses** — `resolveOutboundAttachmentFromUrl` (stage) followed by `loadWebMedia(stagedPath, { hostReadCapability: true })` (the second reload) — on two worktrees that differ by **only this PR's diff**:

- **baseline** = `301213a05f` (this PR's merge-base with `main`; temp-root-only trust gate)
- **candidate** = `2dcfc944` (PR head; content-bound outbound provenance)

The driver writes a generated report under the real OpenClaw temp root, stages it into `media/outbound` (which moves it outside the temp root), then performs the host-read reload exactly as the channel adapter does. Environment: macOS (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0.

```text
# baseline (301213a05f) — same source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[baseline] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[baseline] staged under media/outbound = true
[baseline] staged outside temp root    = true
[baseline] RESULT: REJECTED — staged reload host-read BLOCKED
[baseline]         LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads

# candidate (2dcfc944) — identical source sha256 50fcd4b2…
[candidate] staged path   = …/media/outbound/pr90579-proof-…---<uuid>.html
[candidate] staged under media/outbound = true
[candidate] staged outside temp root    = true
[candidate] RESULT: DELIVERED — staged reload host-read ALLOWED (144 bytes, sha==source? true)
[candidate] TAMPER CHECK: ✅ replaced bytes REJECTED — LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads
```

This is the exact production silent-drop (`LocalMediaAccessError: hostReadCapability permits only validated plain-text documents and trusted generated HTML reports for local reads`) on baseline, and delivery on candidate — with the live tamper step confirming the content binding rejects swapped bytes at the same staged path. It is deterministic, runs in seconds through the real `loadWebMedia` gate, and needs no Telegram client, Mantis SUT, or host-read SUT config. This is the staged-reload-with-host-read path the earlier Mantis run did not exercise (its SUT did not propagate `hostReadCapability`, so both lanes bypassed the gate).

### Original production trace + unit-level confirmation

Behavior addressed: when an agent reply emits `MEDIA:/tmp/openclaw/<file>.html`, OpenClaw's outbound pipeline loads the file once (`/tmp/openclaw/...` is inside the tmp root, so trusted), stages a copy to `~/.openclaw/media/outbound/<file>---<uuid>.html`, and then the Telegram channel adapter calls `loadWebMedia(stagedPath)` a second time. Before this patch the second call rejected because the staged path is no longer under `/tmp/openclaw/`, and the Telegram message was silently dropped. After this patch the staged path is trusted **iff** its bytes match the recorded provenance digest, and delivery proceeds.

Real environment tested: live OpenClaw on macOS 26.4 (Darwin 25.4.0, arm64), Node v26.0.0, Telegram Bot API channel (polling). The original silent-drop was reproduced 4 times on the unpatched build (#90557). For this PR the patched code path was exercised in the repository test harness, since the CI checkout cannot drive a live Telegram bot end-to-end.

Evidence after fix (PR head):

```text
node scripts/generate-kysely-types.mjs --verify
# (exit 0 — generated Kysely types match the schema, incl. sha256 / size_bytes columns)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts
 ✓ media  src/media/web-media.test.ts (79 tests)
 ✓ media  src/media/outbound-attachment.test.ts (5 tests)
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  84 passed (84)
```

Key new coverage:

```text
# Replacement attack (A1): bytes swapped after the marker → rejected
✓ rejects an outbound-staged HTML whose bytes were replaced after the provenance marker (content-bound trust)
# Provenance row records the real sha256 + size_bytes (no hardcoded digest)
✓ writes a trusted-generated-html provenance row keyed by the staged file's realpath
# Marker write failure (A2): propagated + staged file unlinked
✓ propagates a marker write failure and best-effort unlinks the staged file
```

What was not tested from this checkout: live Telegram Bot API delivery, because the CI environment lacks bot credentials. The original silent-drop behavior was verified in production (#90557, 4 reproductions with a `console.error` probe in the installed `dist`); the proof here demonstrates the trusted-host-read gate now accepts the same staged path **only when its bytes match the recorded digest** and rejects a tampered or unmarked staged file. The same instrumented probe can be re-run on a build containing this PR to confirm end-to-end delivery if needed.

target.title: fix(elevenlabs): fall back to default base URL when config value is malformed
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a malformed or non-HTTP(S) ElevenLabs `baseUrl` in provider config is
either crashed on with an uncaught `TypeError: Invalid URL` or silently accepted, instead of
being rejected with an actionable error.

`normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` in `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` only trimmed the value and
stripped trailing slashes — it never confirmed the result was a parseable HTTP(S) URL. Its
callers feed the result straight into `new URL(...)`: `normalizeElevenLabsRealtimeBaseUrl`
(`realtime-transcription-provider.ts:134`) does `new URL(normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl(value))`,
and TTS/speech/media-understanding consume the same helper.

**Concrete example:** with `baseUrl: "not a url"`, `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` on current `main`
returns `"not a url"` unchanged and the downstream `new URL("not a url")` throws an opaque
`TypeError: Invalid URL`. A value like `ftp://files.example.com` parses but is not a usable
ElevenLabs endpoint, yet is accepted and passed to fetch/WebSocket construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Validate the base URL at the shared config boundary and **fail actionably**: only an absent/blank
value falls back to `DEFAULT_ELEVENLABS_BASE_URL`; an explicit value that is unparseable, or whose
scheme is not `http:`/`https:`, throws a clear `Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl` error. This mirrors the
merged `fix(microsoft-foundry): reject malformed endpoints` (#104796) precedent — reject malformed
explicit endpoints rather than silently retargeting them. An operator's explicit custom endpoint is
their intent, so it is never silently swapped for the default (which would change behavior across all
four consumers on upgrade); valid `http(s)` endpoints are trimmed/normalized exactly as before.

## User Impact

**Before:** a mistyped ElevenLabs `baseUrl` surfaces an opaque `TypeError: Invalid URL` at session
setup, and a non-HTTP(S) endpoint is accepted and produces unusable fetch/WebSocket URLs.

**After:** an explicit malformed or non-HTTP(S) `baseUrl` fails fast with an actionable error; absent/blank
config still defaults; valid custom `http(s)` endpoints are unchanged. Validation errors never echo the raw
configured URL, so embedded userinfo or credential-bearing query params are not disclosed to logs/diagnostics.

## Evidence

- `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts` — `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl` rejects explicit malformed / non-HTTP(S) values (throws) and only defaults absent/blank input. Error messages are redacted: the malformed case says "value is not a valid URL"; the scheme case surfaces only the offending `protocol`, never the raw URL.
- Regression test: `extensions/elevenlabs/shared.test.ts` — asserts absent/blank → default, valid → normalized, explicit malformed → throws, `ftp:`/`data:` → throws `unsupported scheme`, and (disclosure test) a `baseUrl` with userinfo + `api_key` query is rejected **without** its secret/token appearing in the error. The malformed/scheme cases fail on the pre-fix `.trim()`-only version; the disclosure test fails on the earlier raw-value error and passes after redaction.
- Function probe against the real production `normalizeElevenLabsBaseUrl`:

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import('./extensions/elevenlabs/shared.ts').then(m => …)"
undefined -> "https://api.elevenlabs.io"
"https://custom.example.com/" -> "https://custom.example.com"
"not a url" -> THROWS: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: value is not a valid URL
"ftp://user:sup3r-secret@files.example.com?api_key=leak-me" -> THROWS: Invalid ElevenLabs baseUrl: unsupported scheme "ftp:" (expected http or https)
```

(The credential-bearing input above is rejected with no `sup3r-secret` / `leak-me` / `api_key` in the message.)

target.title: feat(cloud-workers): replayable worker live-event streaming into the session fanout
target.body:
Part of #104294 (cloud workers, milestone 2, PR 7). Builds on #104688 (worker role) and #104809 (transcript commits). Design: `docs/plan/cloud-workers.md` ("Session backend RPCs" — replayable live events; and `docs/concepts/streaming.md`).

## What Problem This Solves

Transcript commits (PR 6) make a worker session's durable messages appear in the sidebar, but only at turn boundaries. This PR adds the ephemeral, replayable live-event channel so a worker session streams in real time — token deltas, tool start/finish, approvals, run-status — by translating each worker event into the SAME internal agent event and pushing it through the EXISTING fanout, so chat view / tool rows / unread-status behave identically to a local session. No parallel streaming path, no token-delta channel message (per streaming.md). Durable content still arrives via the PR-6 commit path; the live channel never writes transcript entries.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Worker live-event frame on the closed worker allowlist: runEpoch + monotonic worker seq + closed event-kind union (mirroring the local agent-event kinds) + typed payload; gateway cumulative-ACKs. Additive schema, independent feature negotiation, no version bump.
- Gateway application validates credential-session binding and owner epoch (stale/superseded workers fenced), translates to the internal agent event, and publishes through `emitAgentEventForOwner` into the normal fanout.
- Bounded process-local replay window per (session, runEpoch) with cumulative ACK + dedup + late-event fencing; a brief tunnel blip replays only the unacked tail; out-of-window forces a resync; superseded-epoch events never reach subscribers. In-memory only (transient), lifecycle-bounded.

## Deep-review findings fixed pre-merge

A dedicated deep code review (verified independently) found and fixed:
- **Event-loss race (root cause):** the gateway projection is deferred through a Promise while claim release was synchronous. On a mid-drain capacity reset, a just-emitted prefix event's claim could be released before its deferred projection delivered, silently dropping the event in the wired gateway (invisible to receiver-only unit tests). Fixed by keeping a capacity-reset run's claim alive until its in-flight projections settle (`Promise.allSettled`), while detach/supersession teardown stays immediate. Proven by a new gateway+WebSocket integration test asserting exactly-once delivery of a published prefix across a subsequent buffered-capacity event.
- Terminal-run fence retained through projection cleanup so post-terminal events can't resurrect an ended run after window eviction (+ test).
- Speculative `pending` state cleared on in-window resync (prevents a stale buffered event shadowing a renumbered one).
- Collapsed duplicated apply()/resolveWindow validation into one owner (`resolveOrCreateWindow`) and removed a dead epoch branch.
- Bounded fenced-environment LRU refreshes recency on re-fence.
- Added the AGENTS.md-required invariant comments (fence-before-emit ordering, terminalRuns TTL bound, startup-owner cross-filter).

## User Impact

Opt-in only; the worker loop that drives these events lands in PR 9. This is the real-time streaming mechanism for worker sessions. No config/changelog/version-bump changes.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 4 Vitest shards green (live-events receiver incl. capacity-after-prefix and terminal-fence-eviction cases; the new gateway+WS deferred-projection integration test; worker-environments suite; agent-events; server-chat agent-events; worker admission; lint-suppressions).
- Codex fresh autoreview after the fixes: clean, no actionable findings. Local: oxlint (31 files), check:test-types, madge zero cycles, protocol:check, docs:map:check all green.
